title: India DGMO Smiled and Said We Did Not Know. Google Earth Shows an Impact Crater at Pakistan Nuclear Storage Site.
narrative:
India launched Operation Sindoor on the night of May 9-10, 2025, targeting key Pakistani military installations in retaliation for the Pahalgam tourist massacre. The Indian Air Force struck with approximately 15 BrahMos missiles and other precision weapons, reportedly damaging 11 of Pakistan 13 major airbases. When asked at a May 12 press conference whether India had struck Kirana Hills, a heavily fortified area in Pakistan Sargodha district believed to house underground nuclear weapons storage, Director General of Air Operations Air Marshal AK Bharti responded: Thank you for telling us that Kirana Hills houses some nuclear installations. We did not know about it. We have not hit Kirana Hills. I did not brief in my briefing yesterday. His peculiar smile during the denial went viral on Indian social media.

More than two months after that denial, fresh imagery from Google Earth captured in June 2025 appears to tell a different story. Geo-intelligence researcher Damien Symon, whose satellite analysis work on Ukraine, Myanmar, and other conflict zones has gained international recognition, shared the imagery on X on July 18. The Google Earth update of the Sargodha region shows two things: the impact location of India strike on Kirana Hills in May 2025, and repaired runways at Sargodha airbase, now renamed Mushaf airbase, following the Indian strikes.

Kirana Hills is a heavily fortified area associated with Pakistan nuclear weapons program. It reportedly houses underground nuclear weapons storage facilities and was a site for subcritical nuclear tests in the 1980s. The area contains radar stations and military tunnels, and its proximity to Sargodha airbase compounds its strategic significance. The site is considered one of the most sensitive locations in Pakistan nuclear architecture.

Symon analysis notes the imagery does not indicate subterranean impact or penetration, describing it as one side of a hill with nothing of value in its immediate vicinity and characterizing it as must have been a warning strike on India part, tunnels etc are further away and do not show any damage. However, the existence of the strike itself contradicts India categorical denial. The rapid runway repairs at Sargodha airbase further confirm the base sustained damage, reinforcing its status as a high-priority strategic asset.
analysis:
Separately, Symon had earlier debunked Pakistani media claims that Pakistan military had targeted India Adampur airbase, destroying an S-400 system. He provided pre-conflict imagery from March 2025 showing a MiG-29 undergoing routine maintenance, not an S-400. PM Modi later posed at Adampur with an S-400 in the background, confirming its operational status. This track record lends credibility to the Kirana Hills analysis.

The DGMO viral smile was read by Indian social media as a knowing non-denial denial. The satellite imagery confirms what the smile suggested: India struck Kirana Hills, India knew what was there, and the we did not know claim was performative. The angle is not about whether the strike was strategically wise, it is about the gap between India public posture (denial of targeting nuclear assets) and the physical record (Google Earth impact crater at a known nuclear-storage site).

Symon characterization of it as a warning strike is load-bearing: India demonstrated the ability to hit Pakistan nuclear infrastructure without penetrating it, sending a signal that the tunnels could be reached if escalation continued. Pakistan rapid repairs at Sargodha confirm the airbase strategic value. The question for the article: what does Pakistan silence on the Kirana Hills strike tell us about the deterrence dynamics that ended the May 2025 conflict?
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: India DGMO denied striking Kirana Hills with a viral smile. Google Earth imagery from June 2025 shows an impact crater at Pakistan nuclear storage site. Symon calls it a warning strike, India hit the hillside without penetrating the tunnels, demonstrating reach. Pakistan silence on the strike speaks louder than India denial.
